findings.evidence: For `M=[[0,-1],[1,0]]` and `b=0`, `moebiusDenom M 0=0` and `moebiusIdx M 0=0`, but `[1,0;0,p]·M=[[0,-1],[p,0]]`; modulo `p` its nonzero row is `[0,-1]`, the projective infinity point, whereas every upper representative `[1,j;0,p]` has row `[1,j]`. Thus the degenerate input lands in `[p,0;0,1]`, not affine index `0`.
findings.fix: Index all `p+1` representatives by `P¹(ZMod p)` (including `[p,0;0,1]`) and formalize the standard projective Möbius action, then prove that action is a permutation.
findings.issue: The zero-denominator branch `M₁₁/M₁₀` makes an artificial permutation of `ZMod p`; it is not the index induced by right multiplication on `[1,b;0,p]`.

summary: The piecewise permutation is not the claimed action on the affine `T_p` representatives: a pole maps to the missing projective-point representative, not to another affine index.
